s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiovascular syndrome with worsening shortness of breath and chest tightness
key_facts: ECG shows sinus bradycardia with prolonged P-wave duration
ECG shows biphasic P wave morphology in leads II, III, and aVF

raw.syndrome_frame: Cardiovascular syndrome with worsening shortness of breath and chest tightness
key_facts: ECG shows sinus bradycardia with prolonged P-wave duration
ECG shows biphasic P wave morphology in leads II, III, and aVF

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Atrial flutter is present on follow-up ECG, which is a key finding in this case.

shortlist.label: Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of hypertension and presented with high blood pressure (221/85 mm Hg).

shortlist.label: Heart Failure
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, and elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (838.6 pg/mL), which are indicative of heart failure.

shortlist.label: Atrial Fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Although not directly mentioned, atrial fibrillation is a common arrhythmia that can lead to atrial flutter, and the patient's ECG shows biphasic P wave morphology, which can be seen in atrial fibrillation.

shortlist.label: Myocardial Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of chest tightness and shortness of breath, along with elevated B-type natriuretic peptide, could be indicative of myocardial infarction, although it is not directly confirmed.

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, and episodes of palpitations, combined with elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (838.6 pg/mL), left atrial enlargement (52 mm), and mild pulmonary hypertension, are indicative of heart failure.

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: Although atrial flutter is present on the follow-up ECG, it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings.

rejected.label: Hypertension
rejected.why: Hypertension is a contributing factor but does not fully account for the patient's symptoms and other findings such as elevated BNP and left atrial enlargement.

rejected.label: Atrial Fibrillation
rejected.why: There is no evidence of atrial fibrillation in the provided ECG findings, making it an unlikely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: There is no indication of myocardial infarction in the provided information, such as elevated troponin levels or characteristic ECG changes.
